audit.whatIsWrong: 'diff' reads EVEN while diffRating (8/10), breakdown.difficulty and report[14].t all say Hard. Same split as the vayne page.
audit.why: Three fields say hard, one says even, so the enum is the outlier; enum fields are length-exempt and apply cleanly. The seven chart rows themselves agree across full phases[].side, content win[] and packet.levelChart (Yasuo throughout), so no row flips.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level 6 and late spikes describe the right moments but attribute them to the wrong mechanic, and no cooldown is anywhere on the page. Wind Wall is 25/23/21/19/17s for a 4-second wall — the single most trackable timer in the matchup.
audit.why: 'Hold your poke until the wall is spent' is only actionable with the 4-second duration and the cooldown attached. Last Breath's 70/50/30s also matters but the wall is what gates Locke's entire kit.
audit.corrected: 4-second duration added to spikes[1] and mid; the late-game 17s cooldown added to 'late'.

audit.whatIsWrong: The decisive interaction is stated backwards. whys[4], spikes[1], mid and wants.foe[2] all say Purgatory fails because Yasuo airborne-juggles you with Last Breath. The real reason it fails is that Purgatory is a thrown projectile and Wind Wall blocks projectiles outright — the same interaction that eats his Q. Conversely, Purgatory's grounding is Locke's best answer to Yasuo: his E, the Steel Tempest dash and Last Breath are all dashes.
audit.why: Locke's R carries both projectile and grounding flags; Yasuo's W carries blocksProjectiles and his Q/E/R all carry dash. A player told 'the totem doesn't work at 6' plays it as useless; a player told 'the wall blocks it, the grounding beats him' has a sequence.
audit.corrected: Wind Wall blocks Purgatory — throw it only once the wall is spent, and once it lands the grounding removes his E dashes and Last Breath.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page names Locke's Q 'Ritual Nails' in four content fields; Riot's text says he 'readies a set of Soul Nails to throw'.
audit.why: The yasuo-side mirror audit deliberately left this alone as unverified (the display name may differ from the projectile's name), so renaming here would break agreement between the two directions. Left untouched and recorded as unverified.
